records.title: ARA-290
records.description:
ARA-290 (cibinetide) is a synthetic 11–amino acid peptide engineered from the structure of erythropoietin, studied in research for tissue-protective signaling without erythropoietic activity.
Experimental models examine its interaction with the innate repair receptor in inflammatory and neuropathic-pain frameworks.
Overview
ARA-290 is a peptide derived from a region of erythropoietin responsible for tissue protection, designed to engage the innate repair receptor while avoiding the hematopoietic effects of EPO. Research has examined its anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective behavior.
Studies span small-fiber neuropathy, metabolic, and immune-modulation research models under structured conditions.
History
ARA-290 emerged from research separating erythropoietin’s tissue-protective signaling from its erythropoietic activity. The engineered peptide was characterized to retain cytoprotection without raising red-cell mass.
Subsequent clinical and preclinical work investigated neuropathic-pain and metabolic-control endpoints.
Research
Research into ARA-290 focuses on innate-repair-receptor signaling and tissue-protective models. Frameworks evaluate anti-inflammatory activity, neuropathic-pain endpoints, and metabolic regulation under controlled clinical and preclinical conditions.

records.title: HGH (Somatropin)
records.description:
HGH, also known as recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin), is a synthetic peptide hormone identical in sequence to endogenous human growth hormone. It is produced using recombinant DNA technology for controlled laboratory research.
In scientific literature, HGH is studied in experimental models examining growth hormone receptor interaction, endocrine signaling cascades, and downstream cellular response systems under in vitro and preclinical research conditions.
Overview
Recombinant human growth hormone is a 191–amino acid peptide evaluated in research focused on growth hormone receptor activation and endocrine pathway signaling. Experimental studies examine receptor-binding dynamics, IGF-associated pathways, and systemic regulatory frameworks within controlled laboratory environments.
Preclinical and clinical research publications have explored its receptor interaction profile and downstream signaling behavior under structured study conditions.
History
Human growth hormone was originally isolated from pituitary tissue before recombinant DNA technology enabled synthetic production of somatropin. Recombinant HGH became central to endocrine research, allowing for controlled investigation of growth hormone receptor systems and downstream regulatory pathways.
Subsequent research expanded into receptor signaling, metabolic regulation models, and systemic endocrine interaction frameworks.
Research
Laboratory investigations into recombinant human growth hormone have focused on growth hormone receptor activation models and downstream endocrine signaling pathways. Research frameworks evaluate IGF-related signaling cascades, systemic regulatory interaction, and receptor-mediated response systems under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.
